# Custom document actions

Target: NGB 3.4.0. The [deferral example](../examples/equipment-inspection/EquipmentInspection.Runtime/InspectionDeferralDefinitions.cs)
contributes `example.defer-one-day` through `IDocumentActionDefinitionsContributor`.
It advances a draft inspection's date by one day when equipment is selected,
preserves its number and status, and requires a reason. This is application policy,
not a new SDK capability or a change to standard posting.

Register the contributor and every concrete handler/evaluator type in DI, as well
as the context enricher under `IDocumentActionContextEnricher`. The metadata binds
the exact types. Standard lifecycle actions already come from the document's
handler bindings; do not register them a second time alongside a custom action.

## Authorization and availability

A custom non-derivation action without an authorization evaluator defaults to the
document's view permission in 3.4.0. That default does not express permission to
mutate. `InspectionDeferralAuthorization` explicitly requires both source view and
`edit_draft` through `DocumentActionSecurityContext.Has`. This preserves active
administrator semantics and rejects inactive/unauthenticated contexts. Use the
registered permission codes; never infer administrator access from display names.

An authorization evaluator replaces the default decision for that action, so it
must include the relevant source and operation permissions. Omitted actions in
editor state and rejected dispatcher calls enforce the same rule. Do not use a
disabled button as an authorization boundary.

Authorization and availability evaluators are pure and cannot declare constructor
dependencies. Load bounded provider-neutral facts in the one registered context
enricher for the document type. The example checks source view before reading one
inspection and returns only the equipment-selected boolean. Availability consumes
that fact and returns explicit reasons for non-Draft status, missing equipment or
a date that cannot be advanced. It performs no repository or network calls.

An editor-state query loads one fact set. An executed custom action may load the
old state and the refreshed state separately; the example verifies two bounded
reads for execution, not a false promise of one read for the entire request.
Completed idempotent replay refreshes permissions and evaluates the action's
authorization before returning its saved result. When a custom authorization
evaluator is registered, the SDK loads the current document and one current fact
set. It does not rerun the handler or availability evaluator. Keep facts bounded
and free of side effects; the example verifies one fact read for an authorized
repeat, an unchanged document and a single action audit entry.

## Transaction and verification

The handler receives the locked document and joins the dispatcher's transaction.
`IDocumentDraftService.UpdateDraftAsync(..., manageTransaction: false)` retains the
number, advances the UTC date and enforces draft-only mutation. Do not start a
nested transaction, commit independently, update lifecycle status directly or send
external messages from the handler. The dispatcher then increments the document
version, writes its action audit including the reason and correlation, and appends
the completion event atomically.

The [HTTP scenarios](../examples/equipment-inspection/EquipmentInspection.IntegrationTests/InspectionDeferralHttpTests.cs)
exercise real PostgreSQL, Keycloak and public packages. They verify the required
reason, exact one-day change, retained Draft/number, audit attribution, one mutation
under concurrent expected-version requests, and an unchanged result on replay.
A user with view alone can read the document but cannot invoke the action. Disabled
business prerequisites also reject direct HTTP calls. A test handler observes the
updated date inside the transaction before throwing; independent reads then verify
that date, version, audit and execution all rolled back and the same request/key
can succeed on retry. Unit cases cover cancellation, missing facts, the date limit
and inactive/unauthenticated contexts without substituting for provider acceptance.

# Document contracts

Public packages: `NGB.Platform.Core`, `NGB.Platform.Definitions`,
`NGB.Platform.Metadata`, `NGB.Platform.Application.Abstractions`,
`NGB.Platform.Persistence` and `NGB.Platform.PostgreSql` in their respective layers.

`DefinitionsBuilder.AddDocument` accepts a type code and builder configuration.
`DocumentTypeMetadata` describes head/part tables. `DocumentTypeDefinitionBuilder`
supports `AddDraftValidator<T>` and `AddPostValidator<T>` independently.
The generic document read/write service requires a `display` column in head
metadata and storage, even when a custom presentation is configured. Keep it
nullable if an incomplete Draft has no display value yet.
`IDocumentPostValidator.ValidateBeforePostAsync(DocumentRecord, CancellationToken)`
runs with a locked document and an active transaction. Read typed state through an
application-owned interface whose provider implementation uses the current unit
of work. Do not perform unrelated I/O inside the posting transaction.

Accounting, operational-register and reference-register handler bindings are
independent optional properties of `DocumentTypeDefinition`. A document requiring effects must use the relevant
engine's public contract and prove transactionality, retries and reversal history.
Standard Post requires a registered handler, but the handler need not produce
movements. A workflow-only document can explicitly register an
`IDocumentReferenceRegisterPostingHandler` whose `BuildRecordsAsync` completes
without adding records. Post validators, authorization, idempotency and lifecycle
processing still apply. Bind the handler in the document definition and register
its implementation as `IDocumentReferenceRegisterPostingHandler` in DI. This
binding supplies standard Post/Unpost/Repost actions automatically; do not also
register duplicate standard actions manually. No register definition or artificial movement is needed
solely for this lifecycle. The equipment/inspection example's
`InspectionWorkflowDefinitions` and `InspectionWorkflowPostingHandler` demonstrate
that composition through public contracts.

If none of these handlers is registered, automatic Post registration omits the
action. Even explicitly exposing standard Post through
`IDocumentActionDefinitionsContributor` is rejected by the lifecycle with
`doc.posting.handler.not_configured`. The example separately tests this missing
configuration, retaining Draft status and empty effects. This precise limitation
is recorded in `ai/vendor/known-limitations.json`; it does not prohibit successful
Post without movements. Never bypass dispatch or mutate lifecycle status directly.

Interactive callers use `IDocumentActionDispatcher.ExecuteAsync`, including the
action code, idempotency key and `ExecuteDocumentActionRequestDto`. The system
lifecycle port is for trusted server workflows and must not bypass interactive
authorization. `IDocumentService` exposes metadata, Draft CRUD, relationships and
effects. Inspect its resolved signature before implementing an endpoint.

Idempotent replay returns the original action result, including its original
document version; a client must refresh editor state before issuing a new action.
Compare the complete JSON values using `InspectionRequests.AssertEquivalentJsonAsync`
in the example. A stored replay can serialize object properties in a different order.
Reusing a key for a different request returns `document_action.idempotency_conflict`;
a new request with a stale expected version returns `document.version_conflict`.

Successful generic Draft head/part saves and actual common-header changes advance
the action version in the save transaction. Reload editor state after saving;
posting with a version read before that save must fail. This is action concurrency
protection, not optimistic concurrency for the save itself: generic document and
catalog updates have no expected-version argument in 3.4.0. Two stale editors can
still overwrite one another. Do not advertise lost-update protection or invent a
request field that the installed API does not validate.

Treat the returned version as an opaque concurrency token. A custom action that
updates the common header can advance it during both the save and action
completion. Use the returned/refreshed value; do not calculate `oldVersion + 1`.
Replay must retain the committed version and must not repeat the date change.

`DocumentRecord.DateUtc` is the registry's business date; `CreatedAtUtc` is the
creation timestamp. Generic `IDocumentService.CreateDraftAsync` initializes the
registry date from the current clock. A payload field such as `document_date_utc`
is application data and is not automatically bound to the registry date or initial
number allocation. Updating that payload field alone does not move postings made
from `DocumentRecord.DateUtc`. Trusted common-header changes use the existing
`IDocumentDraftService.UpdateDraftAsync`; any interactive workflow needs its
existing authorized application boundary. Do not silently add a date-sync handler,
rewrite historical dates/numbers, or claim that generic CRUD already supplies this
binding. See the explicit 3.4.0 limits in `ai/vendor/known-limitations.json`.

Completed replay refreshes the current actor's permissions before returning the
saved result. It requires an active authenticated actor, source-document View and
the registered action's authorization, including custom evaluators and current
facts. A result containing a created document also requires View of that document.
Denied or deactivated actors receive HTTP 403 even with the complete original
request and idempotency key. The SDK does not execute the handler, check the old
expected version or rerun action availability on a completed replay. The lifecycle
tests also verify that simultaneous identical requests return one execution and
that a denied replay does not prevent an authorized caller from receiving it.
Earlier 3.4.0 candidate failures remain recorded in the historical reports.

`PostgresHeadDocumentTypeStorage` supports a simple head table keyed by
`document_id`. More complex typed storage implements the public persistence
contract. Migrations and storage belong in the provider project. The independent
equipment/inspection example verifies the minimal contract; its test report must
identify separately which unit, HTTP, persistence and browser outcomes ran.

For a custom mutation with explicit permissions, pure availability rules, bounded
context facts and transaction composition, read [custom document actions](custom-document-actions.md).

## Numbering, lookup and document composition

Bind `IDocumentNumberingPolicy` through `NumberingPolicy<T>` and register the same
implementation by concrete type and interface in DI. The inspection policy assigns
numbers on Draft creation; the SDK allocates and formats them. Eight concurrent
creates produce distinct numbers, and failed Post, Post, Repost and Unpost retain
the original number. Do not allocate a number in an API controller or derive it
from the current row count.

Document pages use explicit `limit`, `cursor` and `includeTotal` parameters. Follow
the returned cursor without interpreting it, and keep search and other filters
unchanged between pages. The HTTP controller requires total-count opt-in even
though the DTO's constructor has a different default. Cross-type lookup accepts
`DocumentLookupAcrossTypesRequestDto` at `POST /api/documents/lookup`; its limit is
per type. Lookup filters types by the distinct `Lookup` permission. `View` alone
does not grant lookup, and a request with no permitted types returns an empty list.

`InspectionDerivationDefinitions` registers `example.reinspect` and a directed
ManyToOne relationship. The derivation's code is the action code; no prefix is
added. Dispatching it creates one numbered Draft, its domain relationship and a
standard `created_from` child-to-source edge in the same transaction. The latter
makes the chain visible to the shared Document Flow UI. The target inherits the
source registry date. With no derivation handler, it has no copied application
fields and is not automatically Posted.
An optional `NGB.Runtime.Documents.Derivations.IDocumentDerivationHandler` receives
the source and target in `DocumentDerivationContext` within that transaction.
Keep any prefill work inside the existing unit of work and register the handler
declared by the definition. This example intentionally uses no prefill handler.

The derivation requires source View and target View/Create. An unavailable action
is omitted from the editor action list; a direct unauthorized invocation is also
denied. Replaying the same authorized request returns the existing target. The
relationship service separately enforces allowed endpoint types and cardinality;
adding the same edge again is an idempotent no-op. Its trusted server methods are
not an interactive permission boundary. Use authorized application services for
interactive operations.

Graph reads require View and ViewFlow on the root. The returned graph excludes
inaccessible document types and their edges. Use explicit depth and node bounds.
A bidirectional relationship persists both directions; this is separate from a
head reference field's `MirroredDocumentRelationshipMetadata`. A mirrored field
must be a Guid document lookup on the head table with a registered relationship
and compatible endpoint types. The fixture checks rejection of an invalid String
mirror at startup; it does not claim field synchronization acceptance for that
invalid definition.

`ExtendDocument` adds bindings while preserving the original metadata. Extend
relationship and derivation definitions by their existing codes. The contract
tests verify preservation of endpoints, cardinality and identity after renaming,
and rejection of unknown extensions, duplicate identities and conflicting bindings.

## Head/part storage and separate validation boundaries

The `example.inspection-checklist` API example declares one head table and a
`checks` part. Use an explicit `PartCode`; the payload is keyed by that code, not
the physical table name. The provider owns an embedded immutable migration and
`ChecklistStorage`, bound through a provider contributor's `TypedStorage<T>`.
Register that implementation by concrete type and `IDocumentTypeStorage`. Its
methods require the caller's active unit of work. Creation inserts the typed head;
Draft deletion removes the head and its application-owned cascading child rows.
The standard parts writer replaces the submitted part inside the same transaction.

Omitting `Parts` preserves existing rows. Sending `checks` with an empty `Rows`
list clears that part. Clients cannot supply row `document_id`, unknown part codes
or undeclared columns. The checklist requires positive unique `line_no` values,
while descriptions and results may remain empty in Draft. Acceptance crosses the
provider's batch boundary with 501 rows and injects failure after real head, part
and audit writes to verify rollback. Do not issue independent commits from typed
storage, validators or posting handlers.

Draft validation has two public contracts. `IDocumentDraftValidator` receives
common registry fields, and the trusted Draft service also calls it for header
updates. The example prohibits future observation dates; it does not require a
finished checklist. `NGB.Runtime.Documents.Validation.IDocumentDraftPayloadValidator`
receives incoming payload and converted part rows during generic Draft create
and update. Register it as that interface in DI; `AddDraftValidator<T>` is for the
registry validator, not the payload validator. Missing parts on update are not a
request to clear them.

`ChecklistPostValidator` checks persisted completeness: at least one check must
have a description and a result, and every supplied check must be complete. A
false result is a completed observation, so it does not prevent recording the
checklist. `ChecklistApprovalPolicy` separately requires persisted `reviewed=true`.
The public `ApprovalPolicy<T>` binding and resolver describe and resolve a policy;
generic Post does not automatically invoke it. This example's Post validator
explicitly resolves and calls the registered policy before posting, and rejects
a missing binding. Keep that invocation in the same transaction as posting.

The review flag is this example's completion condition, editable under the normal
Draft permission. It is not a separate approver identity, signature or segregation
of duties workflow. Applications needing those rules must implement their own
authorized transitions and persisted state through supported contracts. The
example exercises both administrator kinds without manual grants. It exposes the
checklist through the generic API; its web fixture does not implement a tabular
checklist editor.

### Draft text limits

In SDK 3.4.0, document metadata `MaxLength` describes the field and checks schema
compatibility; the generic Draft writer does not enforce that length on input.
Map `ColumnType.String` to PostgreSQL `text`, even when metadata has `MaxLength`.
`varchar(n)` fails the SDK's physical schema validation. Enforce a database length
limit with `CHECK (char_length(column) <= limit)`. That constraint alone can produce
HTTP 500 for an oversized value, so also reject invalid input before persistence.
See [physical schema validation](persistence.md#typed-schema-validation-and-posted-document-guards).

Use `NGB.Runtime.Documents.Validation.IDocumentDraftPayloadValidator` in the
application Runtime project. Implement **both** `ValidateCreateDraftPayloadAsync`
and `ValidateUpdateDraftPayloadAsync`, expose the document's exact `TypeCode`, and
register it with `services.AddScoped<IDocumentDraftPayloadValidator, YourValidator>()`.
This interface is resolved from DI; `AddDraftValidator<T>` binds a different
contract for common registry fields and does not register a payload validator.

The working [ChecklistPayloadValidator](../examples/equipment-inspection/EquipmentInspection.Runtime/ChecklistPayloadValidator.cs)
validates optional head and part text on both paths. Its limit comes from the
same Definitions constant as metadata. Head `payload.Fields` values are raw
`JsonElement`s; match names case-insensitively, preserve omitted fields on partial
updates, and allow null/empty/whitespace when Draft permits them. The generic
String conversion accepts other JSON values as text; validate that converted
representation too. Part rows supplied to the validator are already typed.
Throw `NgbArgumentInvalidException` with the field name for HTTP 400; do not
truncate or silently normalize saved text.

Post completeness remains separate: an optional completion note may have a Draft
length limit and require nonwhitespace persisted text only at Post. A Post
validator cannot protect Draft create/update. Run HTTP tests for the exact limit,
one character over it on **both** create and update, nullable Draft values and
omitted-field updates. Rejected writes must leave saved fields, parts, version,
audit and document count unchanged. See
[ChecklistHttpTests](../examples/equipment-inspection/EquipmentInspection.IntegrationTests/ChecklistHttpTests.cs).

## Database protection of posted typed records

Install the platform's existing typed-document guards after the application's
head/part tables are created; see [typed schema validation](persistence.md#typed-schema-validation-and-posted-document-guards).
A correct HTTP lifecycle does not by itself establish database protection against
an incorrect trusted storage call. `TypedDocumentGuardTests` verifies that direct
typed deletion of a Posted inspection or checklist fails, rolls back and preserves
head/parts/audit, while public Unpost restores Draft editing. This is a provider
invariant check, not additional user permission or a new posting behavior.


## Interactive actions and trusted lifecycle ports

Use `IAuthorizedDocumentReadService` for interactive metadata, pages, lookups,
effects and relationship reads. `IDocumentActionQueryService` returns editor
state and action availability; this is a snapshot, so execution must still go
through `IDocumentActionDispatcher` with the version and idempotency contract.

The older `IDocumentService.ExecuteActionAsync` overload taking only a string
action code throws `DocumentActionsNotSupportedException` in the current SDK.
This does not mean document actions are absent. The standard controller uses
the dispatcher. Do not route a new adapter to the similarly named legacy method.

`IDocumentSystemLifecycleService` is explicitly for trusted seeders, migrators and
background workflows. Exposing it directly in an interactive adapter would omit
the dispatcher's user-facing action contract. Neither a stored technical success
nor construction of a request supplies current-user authorization.

## Trusted batch workflows and number formatting

Resolve `IDocumentDraftService` or `IDocumentPostingService` and inspect whether
the instance implements `IDocumentDraftBatchService` or
`IDocumentPostingBatchService`. The standard container registers the base
interfaces; do not assume the optional interfaces can be resolved directly.
These are trusted server workflows, not a public interactive batch API.

Draft creation accepts at most 1000 common-header requests with UTC dates. The
standard workflow retains registered validation, typed storage, audit and
transactional numbering. Optional provider batch ports can reduce round trips,
with the existing per-item fallback when unavailable. `manageTransaction: false`
requires an active caller-owned transaction, including rollback on failure.

Posting accepts at most 25 distinct IDs, deduplicates while retaining input order,
and applies the batch in one transaction. Optional prefetchers only prime immutable
posting reads in that transaction; they do not apply effects. A posting read cache
must remain operation-local and must not retain stale data across later edits.

`IDocumentNumberFormatter` receives type, fiscal year and reserved sequence. Keep
formatting deterministic and stable; it must not reserve a second number. A
type-specific decorator can retain `DefaultDocumentNumberFormatter` for other
types. The batch allocator owns reservations by type/year in the Draft transaction.
Typed header synchronization also stays in that transaction.

`DocumentBatchTests` creates two workflow-only inspections under an external
transaction, then rolls back and confirms that the next batch reuses its reserved
numbers. Its formatter adds an example prefix only for inspections. An incomplete
second document rolls back the first Post; after correction both post, duplicate
IDs are ignored and repetition retains Posted state. Separate checks exercise
the batch limits, empty input and cancellation. These small examples establish
atomic lifecycle behavior, not throughput or all combinations of register effects.

## Runtime action and relationship internals

The startup action registry combines standard actions, declared derivations and
application contributors. It validates handler identities and presentation order;
advertising an action does not authorize its execution. Keep interactive calls
on the action dispatcher. The derivation service creates a target Draft using the
registered relationship semantics; it does not automatically post that target.

Relationship repositories and graph readers are lower-level storage/read services.
Document-flow access must retain current document permissions and registered
relationship rules. The action-execution repository stores request identity,
fingerprint and a recorded result; it does not itself reauthorize a replay. The
action dispatcher checks current authorization before returning that result.
Storage idempotency alone does not prove current authorization.

## Batch relationships and provider list filters

The resolved `IDocumentRelationshipService` may implement
`IDocumentRelationshipBatchService`. `CreateManyAsync` accepts at most 1000 input
requests, checks registered types, Draft requirements, cardinality and cycles,
then writes relationships and audit in one transaction. Repeated identical edges
do not create extra audit records. With `manageTransaction: false`, the caller
must own an active transaction and roll it back on failure. This is a trusted
server operation; do not expose it as an unauthenticated bulk endpoint.

`DocumentRelationshipBatchTests` verifies caller rollback, duplicate edges,
existing cardinality conflicts, a cycle entirely inside a proposed batch, bounds
and cancellation. Its HTTP graph check still requires document-flow permission.
The fixture does not establish concurrent relationship throughput or every
bidirectional topology.

A declared `DocumentListFilterMetadata` maps directly to a head column when
configured or when its key matches that column. Otherwise the PostgreSQL reader
asks `IPostgresDocumentListFilterSqlContributor` implementations in registration
order. Match the exact owned document type and filter key; return false for other
filters. Construct SQL expressions from trusted provider code and bind values
with `DynamicParameters`/`PostgresDocumentFilterSql`. Never concatenate a user
filter value into SQL. Register the contributor in the provider/host layer.

`DocumentListFilterTests` supplies an explicit case-insensitive result filter,
verifies a literal SQL-looking input returns no matches, rejects undeclared keys
before the contributor, preserves direct-column filtering and denies an ungranted
reader before query execution. Query parameters use `filters.result_label` (or
the plain key), not bracket notation. Adding the contributor alone does not
advertise a filter; declare it in the application's original document metadata.

## Withdrawal and dependent documents

A Reference Register handler builds register records. It is not a universal
lifecycle validator. In 3.4.0, Unpost returns from the RR branch before resolving
the handler when no register write state exists for the document. An empty
handler can enable Post but cannot be relied on to reject withdrawal. Repost
also has different semantics; do not treat it as an Unpost callback. Never create
fake RR records to force a business guard to run.

Define correction rules from the business workflow and prove them through the
actual authorized action/API path. Rejected withdrawal must preserve status,
version and all financial/operational effects. Include a dependent Posted record,
repeat requests and a competing dependent write using the same locking policy.
A unit test calling the guard directly is insufficient.

For custom actions, context facts and availability evaluators are rechecked by
`IDocumentActionDispatcher` inside its transaction. Mutation-time invariants must
also be checked by the supported application handler under the relevant locks;
UI action availability is only a snapshot. Follow [custom actions](custom-document-actions.md).
Do not assume a custom action guards the standard Unpost/Repost routes or trusted
system lifecycle calls. The current registry creates standard actions first;
adding another definition under the same type/action key is a duplicate, not an
override API. Inspect supported contracts for every reachable path. If a required
guard cannot be installed through them, report that concrete limitation and keep
acceptance incomplete instead of inventing a hook or changing Platform implicitly.

## Visible Document Flow

The shared Document Flow UI displays standard relationship codes `based_on`,
`created_from`, `reversal_of`, `related_to` and `supersedes`. Select one according
to the business relationship and preserve its source/target direction. Register
compatible endpoint types/cardinality and create the edge in the same transaction
as the linked document, using a derivation, supported head-field mirror or the
public relationship service as appropriate. A document lookup by itself is not
an edge.

A custom domain relationship may coexist with a standard flow relationship. It
must not replace the standard edge if the chain should appear in the shared UI.
Do not broaden shared UI filtering merely because a generated application used
only custom codes. For a new derivation, use the semantic standard relationship;
for an existing persisted domain relationship, preserve its code and add the
standard edge through the authorized workflow rather than renaming history.

Verify a source/child/grandchild chain both in the authorized graph response and
in the actual browser page, including link navigation and excluded inaccessible
nodes. A passing graph API test alone cannot prove visible hierarchy.

# Application errors and HTTP boundaries

Target: NGB 3.4.0. Use the public
[Tools error contracts](contracts/NGB.Platform.Tools.json) and
[ASP.NET Core hosting contracts](contracts/NGB.Platform.Hosting.AspNetCore.json).

Runtime errors stay independent of HTTP. `INgbError` supplies a stable
`ErrorCode`, `Kind` and structured `Context`. Derive an application-specific
exception from the appropriate `NgbValidationException`, `NgbNotFoundException`,
`NgbConflictException` or `NgbForbiddenException` base when the workflow needs its
own stable code. The predefined required/invalid/out-of-range argument exceptions
already carry field identity for the standard validation response. Do not use a
configuration or invariant failure to represent normal incomplete Draft input.

`NgbExceptionPolicy.Apply` preserves cancellation, existing structured NGB errors
and provider `DbException` instances. It wraps a timeout with `ngb.infra.timeout`
and other unexpected failures with `ngb.unexpected`, preserving the original as
`InnerException`. These wrappers omit the original message from their public
message and context. Additional context is copied as supplied: include only
deliberately public, bounded values. `Exception.ToString()`, `InnerException`,
raw provider diagnostics and arbitrary context are not safe HTTP response bodies.
The policy is not a general-purpose secret scrubber.

Keep the template's `AddGlobalErrorHandling` registration and exception-handler
middleware. The standard HTTP response uses `application/problem+json`, a stable
`error.code`/`error.kind`, the request `instance` and a `traceId`. Field validation
includes `error.errors` and normalized `error.issues`. Consumers should handle
codes and fields rather than parsing the English detail message.

| Error kind | Default HTTP status |
| --- | --- |
| Validation | 400 |
| NotFound | 404 |
| Conflict | 409 |
| Forbidden | 403 |
| Configuration, Infrastructure, unexpected fallback | 500 |
| Explicit timeout | 504 |

Non-5xx structured errors expose their chosen message. Server failures use a
generic detail; structured context remains the application's responsibility.
Raising a forbidden error is only a transport signal, not an implementation of
authorization. Existing current-user application services still decide access.

Provider-specific translation belongs at the host composition boundary through
`INgbExceptionHttpMapper`. Return a supported status, stable code/kind and safe
context for a recognized provider failure; return null for unrelated exceptions.
Keep provider dependencies out of Runtime. Do not map an unknown storage failure
to a successful business result or replace the platform's authorization checks.

The independent `ErrorBoundaryContractTests` exercise the real Production HTTP
middleware on a loopback server. They verify argument and application error
families, field details, tracing, timeout/fallback behavior and a synthetic
provider mapper returning 503. Separate policy checks preserve cancellation and
provider exception identity while retaining private messages only in the inner
exception. The fixture does not expose a business endpoint or prove arbitrary
application context is sanitized; real provider/network failures have their own
integration scenarios.

than writing statuses in the client. Feature flags and access checks control

through supported props/slots and application-owned composition. Avoid copying a
private component merely to change a visual detail. If the public component lacks
the requested extension, report the precise missing contract.

and disposable Keycloak; component mocks alone cannot prove authorization.

The starter's `web/src/` and test configuration are a small working example.

not arbitrary future business forms or all framework component combinations.

actual SignalR delivery, then exercises dismiss, snooze and saved preferences

pages. Importing a loader does not mean invoking it eagerly during bootstrap.

uses `NgbPageHeader` from `@ngbplatform/ui/layout` to display a useful unknown-page
message and an explicit return action.

Navigation configuration comes from `@ngbplatform/ui/navigation`; the site's
Work Center button opens its drawer and **View all** follows the configured
full-page route. The production browser test exercises that path, theme switching,

The packaged styles and preset supply real computed colors and layout; the
`vite-public-assets` plugin supplies `favicon.svg` and `silent-check-sso.html` in

Node-side browser tests use type-only imports from `@ngbplatform/ui/contracts`.
The published UI runtime is TypeScript for the application's Vite build; Node 24

When browser-mode Vitest tests import additional package subpaths, predeclare

tests. The example's current configuration covers its ten source files; it does

Application startup is an explicit `startApplication` function in `src/bootstrap.ts`.
The browser entry `src/main.ts` calls it once. Tests invoke the function directly
for each authentication, access and failure case, so they do not depend on
re-evaluating a cached browser module. Keep metadata capability assertions on

## Document Lines

Import `NgbDocumentLines` and `DocumentLinesColumn`/`DocumentLinesHandle` from
`@ngbplatform/ui/editor` (also exported at the package root). This is the standard
tabular editor surface: title, fixed columns, dotted separators, row numbers,
validation, bounded pages, add/delete and local drag or Alt+Arrow reordering.
It has no dependency on an application's document types or calculations.

Supply `rows`, `columns` (`key`, `label`, optional `width`/`align`), a stable
`rowKey`, `readonly` and structural permissions `allowAddRemoveRows`/`allowReorder`.
The `cell` slot receives `row`, global `rowIndex`, `column` and `readonly`.
Render public grid-variant inputs, lookups and selects there, respecting field
read-only rules as well as the document state. The `header` and `footer` slots
support business explanations and calculated totals without replacing the table.

The component emits `add`, `remove(rowIndex)` and `reorder(fromIndex, toIndex)`;
the owner creates/clones rows, preserves identities, renumbers its ordering field
and emits the existing payload. It never mutates input rows. Apply calculations,
lookup defaults and business rules in that owner; do not move them into the SDK.
Indices refer to the full row array, including on later pages. Default page size
is 100. Keep errors keyed by global row index and column key; values can be a
message or a list of messages. `summaryErrors` is separate. The exposed
`focusCell`/`focusFirstError` methods reveal a later page before focusing its cell.

```vue
<NgbDocumentLines
  title="Lines"
  :rows="rows"
  :columns="columns"
  :row-key="row => row.id"
  :readonly="readonly"
  :errors="errors"
  @add="addRow"
  @remove="removeRow"
  @reorder="reorderRows"
>
  <template #cell="{ row, rowIndex, column }">
    <NgbInput
      :model-value="row[column.key]"
      :readonly="readonly"
      variant="grid"
      @update:model-value="value => updateCell(rowIndex, column.key, value)"
    />
  </template>
</NgbDocumentLines>
```

Use the existing `documentPartsEditor` configuration or entity-editor render
extension to mount the application owner. Preserve its public props/events,
payload shape and persistence strategy when migrating an existing editor.
Keep lookup navigation available in view mode. Verify save/reload, calculated
values, validation focus, row identity after reorder and paging, and readonly
behavior. The component is additive; existing custom editors remain supported.

## Branding integration

# Independent reference-register writes and time

Target: NGB 3.4.0. Use the public
[Runtime](contracts/NGB.Platform.Runtime.json) and
[ReferenceRegisters](contracts/NGB.Platform.ReferenceRegisters.json) contracts.
The executable example is
[IndependentReferenceRegisterTests.cs](../examples/equipment-inspection/EquipmentInspection.IntegrationTests/IndependentReferenceRegisterTests.cs).

## Ownership and commands

Configure `ReferenceRegisterRecordMode.Independent` with explicit fields and
dimension rules through `IReferenceRegisterManagementService`, then ensure its
physical schema through `IReferenceRegisterAdminMaintenanceService`. There is
no recorder document. A subordinate register instead uses the document lifecycle;
the independent write service rejects that mode.

`IReferenceRegisterIndependentWriteService` is a trusted application service,
not an HTTP authorization boundary. Authorize the caller and validate application
rules before invoking it from an application operation. Do not add an unrestricted
endpoint exposing arbitrary register IDs. The example invokes these contracts
inside its disposable, trusted test fixture; it does not claim UI or HTTP mutation
coverage for independent registers.

Upsert appends a version; it does not update an existing row. Supply a stable
`commandId` when retrying the same logical operation. Idempotency is scoped to
register, command and operation, and returns `Executed` or `AlreadyCompleted`.
It is not a payload-comparison contract: do not reuse a completed command ID for
different content. Use a new command for an intentional correction.

The default `manageTransaction=true` owns the transaction. For a larger atomic
application operation, begin one unit-of-work transaction and pass
`manageTransaction=false` to every participating call. The service rejects that
mode without an active transaction, and rejects transaction ownership when one is
already active. Records, command completion and audit commit or roll back together.
Keep network calls and other nontransactional side effects outside this scope.

## Periods and historical reads

Nonperiodic records require a null period. Periodic records require a UTC instant.
Supported buckets are second, day, month, quarter and year. The stored original
`PeriodUtc` and normalized `PeriodBucketUtc` are distinct; a monthly bucket does
not make a change effective from the first day of its month.

`SliceLast*` uses one `asOfUtc` for both effective time and recorded time. A periodic
record must have `PeriodUtc <= asOfUtc` and `RecordedAtUtc <= asOfUtc`. Within the
selected key, ordering considers bucket, original period, recorded timestamp and
record ID. A future effective record cannot hide the earlier applicable value.
A correction recorded today is not visible in a query for yesterday, even when
its effective period is earlier. These signatures do not expose independent
effective-time and knowledge-time parameters.

`GetKeyHistory*` requires `periodUtc` for a periodic register and forbids it for
a nonperiodic one. The argument selects a bucket, not an exact instant. Query
each required bucket explicitly. Page versions using both
`beforeRecordedAtUtc` and `beforeRecordId`, keeping the same as-of bound across
pages. The example verifies previous-month rates, corrections, two future rates
in one month and the original state before the correction was recorded.

## Tombstones and paging

Tombstone selects the applicable latest version at the supplied effective time
and appends a deleted version with that record's original period and values.
The argument is not a new deletion-effective date. A missing or already-deleted
key is a completed no-op; a successful logical deletion retains its prior values
and history. A later effective record remains independently applicable. To model
a different business concept such as an explicit end date, first verify that the
application's chosen data model expresses it.

By default reads hide the selected tombstone and do not fall back to an older
visible version. Use `includeDeleted` explicitly for history and diagnostics.
For current-state paging use the cursor-aware `SliceLastAll*PageAsync` methods
and their `NextAfterDimensionSetId`/`HasMore`. A cursor advances by examined keys,
which can include deleted keys, rather than necessarily the last returned row.
Keep a fixed as-of, obey the limit and stop on `HasMore=false`. The example checks
multiple pages across deleted equipment keys, dimension filtering and enriched
display values, plus concurrent retries and rollback of records and audit.

# Runtime MCP and AI Assistant integration

Target: NGB 3.4.0, preserving the read-only runtime MCP contract introduced in 3.3.
Use [MCP](contracts/NGB.Platform.Mcp.json),
[MCP hosting](contracts/NGB.Platform.Mcp.AspNetCore.json),
[Assistant](contracts/NGB.Platform.AiAssistant.json) and
[Assistant hosting](contracts/NGB.Platform.AiAssistant.AspNetCore.json).

Enable runtime features only through explicit application configuration. The Kit
itself needs neither a running MCP server nor a model provider. CLI development
commands never become production MCP tools.

Register a custom typed read tool with `AddNgbMcpContributor<TContributor>`.
Its `IMcpReadToolContributor.Contribute` calls the registry builder's
`Add<TRequest,TResult,THandler>` with a stable name, description and permission
keys. Implement `IMcpReadToolHandler<TRequest,TResult>` as a bounded, side-effect
free operation over an existing authorized application service. Registration
permissions do not replace object-level access. Do not accept arbitrary SQL,
filesystem commands, database credentials or unrestricted identifiers as tools.

`IMcpReadSourceProvider<TRequest,TResult>` provides explicit source attribution.
Do not interpret arbitrary payload text as an authoritative source or instruction.
Handle feature availability, cancellation and bounded response sizes explicitly.

### Public host composition

Reference `NGB.Platform.Mcp.AspNetCore` at the application's exact platform
version. Register the concrete handler in the request scope, register its
contributor with `AddNgbMcpContributor<TContributor>`, and call
`AddNgbMcp(configuration)` after the existing application services. Map
`MapNgbMcp()` after the normal authentication and authorization middleware.
`FeatureManagement:Mcp` defaults to disabled. Opting out leaves no MCP route;
configuration reload does not dynamically add one.

Set `Ngb:Hosting:PublicApiUrl` to the externally visible API origin. An explicit
`Mcp:Resource` override must match the mapped endpoint, including its path.
Configure trusted proxy forwarding in the host so the request authority matches
that resource. HTTPS is required; `Mcp:AllowLocalhostHttp` is only for local
development. Browser callers need an exact origin in `Mcp:AllowedOrigins` unless
they share the resource origin. `Mcp:AuthenticationScheme` defaults to the
existing API `Bearer` scheme; do not install a second permissive JWT validator.

The endpoint requires a bearer header and an active current-user access snapshot.
Its token policy also requires a subject, `typ=Bearer` and positive `auth_time`;
client credentials and service-account identities are not interactive users.
Use the provider's authorization-code flow with PKCE. A password-grant token
that authenticates ordinary API requests does not necessarily satisfy this MCP
policy. Never invent claims or bypass issuer, audience, signature or lifetime
validation in an adapter. An ordinary user needs an active application record;
the existing trusted administrator path also supports an unlinked administrator.

Transport options bound the whole request: `MaxRequestBytes` defaults to 128 KiB,
`ConcurrentRequests` to 24, `RequestsPerMinute` to 120 and
`RequestTimeoutSeconds` to 45. The separate `Mcp:Reads` section defaults to
64 KiB of tool arguments, 1 MiB of serialized response, 100 registered tools,
JSON depth 32, 1,000 record rows and 256 KiB of record storage JSON. These are
deployment budgets, not permission grants. Application query limits still apply;
custom tools must use bounded reads and propagate cancellation themselves.

### Independent typed read example

The [equipment example](../examples/equipment-inspection/README.md) registers
`example_get_equipment` with a typed `{ id }` input and a catalog-view permission.
`EquipmentReadTool` delegates to `IAuthorizedCatalogReadService.GetByIdAsync`
and returns only the saved ID/name. It does not call a repository or execute SQL.
Its source provider constructs a `McpReadSource` from that authorized result.
The SDK wraps it in `McpReadResponse<T>` with schema version, generation time,
data and sources; arbitrary strings in the record never become tool instructions.
`McpReadException` represents a bounded tool error, not permission to expose
internal exception details.

The HTTP tests start the actual endpoint, PostgreSQL and Keycloak. They exercise
discovery, a successful read, explicit sources, malformed/missing IDs, argument
and body limits, inactive/anonymous identities, denied origins and feature opt-out.
An active reader first cannot discover or call the tool; a grant through the
public security API permits the same request. Payload text asking for a deletion
is returned as data, the named deletion tool does not exist, and the object's
stored representation and audit remain unchanged. Cancellation is also checked
on the concrete handler. This is a deterministic adapter check, not a claim about
every model's behavior under prompt injection or every network failure mode.

### Built-in authorized reads

Use the reserved names in `McpToolNames`; do not replace them with application
handlers. `ngb_get_capabilities` and `ngb_list_metadata` discover the current
user's available reads. `ngb_get_metadata` returns definitions with mutation
actions and capability controls stripped. Discovery is bounded with offset/limit;
record lists use the underlying authorized service's cursor and filter contract.
`ngb_get_record` preserves the catalog or document DTO and adds its canonical
source, type name and lookup-field metadata. The detail read is bounded by the
configured row/byte budget before materialization.

`ngb_search` returns explicit partial-result flags and unavailable source names.
Use a declared kind/type to narrow a search. The compatibility `search` tool
cannot represent partial results and returns `source_unavailable` when any source
fails. Its result and compatibility `fetch` are direct compatibility objects,
without the ordinary `McpReadResponse<T>` envelope. Fetch accepts canonical
`kind:typeCode:id` source IDs or `report:reportCode`; it does not fetch arbitrary
URLs. Report fetch returns the authorized definition, not executed report rows.

`ConfiguredMcpNgbLinkResolver` maps canonical sources to explicitly configured
routes on one trusted HTTPS UI origin. Supply supported source-kind keys and
local route patterns with `{typeCode}` and `{id}` placeholders as appropriate.
An unconfigured route has no link. Do not infer routes from record text or treat
a link as an authorization grant.

`ngb_get_document_flow` delegates to the existing bounded relationship reader.
`ngb_get_document_effects` returns current effects with result-local identifiers.
Preserve `Completeness`: reaching a per-family limit produces `unknown_at_limit`,
not proof that all effects were returned. Read the authorized report definition
before `ngb_execute_report`: declared parameters belong in `request.parameters`
as strings, and declared filters in `request.filters` as objects with `value`.
Underlying date, paging and cursor rules still apply. The MCP report limit is at
most 200. A definition response is not evidence that report execution succeeded.

Content tools use the canonical business-object target and existing feature and
permission checks. `ngb_list_notes` pages literal note text as untrusted data.
`ngb_list_attachments` exposes Ready attachment metadata, without file bytes,
storage keys or download URLs; pending uploads are absent. Disabled content
features can have null counts in `ngb_get_content_summary`.
`ngb_get_audit_history` returns a bounded audit selection.
`ngb_get_work_items` returns the current recipient's page or summary without
marking notifications read. Its DTO omits executable targets and primary actions.
These reads do not perform a lifecycle transition or a work-item command.

The built-in General Journal Entry supports discovery, metadata, list, detail
and compatibility `fetch` in 3.4.0. Metadata inspection does not require the
storage descriptor used by generic document CRUD. Detail reads reuse the existing
`IAuthorizedGeneralJournalEntryReadService` and its current-user permission checks.
No journal storage fields or lifecycle paths are added. See
[`mcp.general-journal-detail`](../known-limitations.json).

`McpBuiltInReadTests` exercises all 18 built-in names through the actual HTTP
endpoint. Known records, reports, note/audit pages, unread notifications and a
real object-storage upload establish the returned identities and unchanged state.
Both administrator identities are checked, and a reader receives catalog search
only after public permission grants. A separate case verifies journal metadata/detail, compatibility fetch and
denied access alongside the dedicated HTTP read. These cases do not establish every
filter shape, transport, deployment limit or model response.

### Assistant providers

Reference `NGB.Platform.AiAssistant.AspNetCore` and the chosen public provider
package at the application's exact platform version. Set both
`FeatureManagement:AiAssistant` and `FeatureManagement:Mcp` to `true`; Assistant
without the MCP feature fails configuration. Pass provider registration to the
`AddNgbAiAssistant(configuration, configureProvider)` callback. The callback runs
only when Assistant is enabled and must register an `IChatClient`. Register
exactly one provider; the SDK does not choose one from a provider-name setting.

The example's `EquipmentAssistant` adds an application-owned `AiAssistant:Provider`
selector with the exact values below. This selector is example composition, not a
new SDK setting. Unknown or missing selections fail when the feature is enabled.
The example references all four adapters to make their integration executable;
an application that supports one provider can reference and register only that one.

| Selection | Public registration | Server configuration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OpenAI` | `AddNgbOpenAiChatClient` | `AiAssistant:OpenAI`: required `Model` and `ApiKey`; optional HTTPS `Endpoint`, default `https://api.openai.com/v1` |
| `Anthropic` | `AddNgbAnthropicChatClient` | `AiAssistant:Anthropic`: required `Model` and `ApiKey` |
| `Bedrock` | `AddNgbBedrockChatClient` | `AiAssistant:Bedrock`: required known AWS `Region` and `Model`/inference profile; credentials use the AWS SDK chain |
| `Ollama` | `AddNgbOllamaChatClient` | `AiAssistant:Ollama`: local `Model`, `Endpoint` and bounded `ContextLength`; remote HTTP requires explicit `AllowInsecureHttp` |

Bind the selected section to its public options type. Validation runs at host
startup. Cloud endpoint URLs must not contain user information, queries or
fragments. The Ollama adapter rejects cloud models; loopback HTTP is allowed,
while remote HTTP is an explicit trusted-network choice. Prefer a workload role
for Bedrock. Supply cloud keys through server secret configuration, never browser
runtime configuration, committed application settings or CLI evidence.

Map `MapNgbAiAssistant()` after `MapNgbMcp()` and normal authentication/
authorization middleware. The mapped MCP resource must be reachable from the API.
The Assistant opens its own request-owned connection with the caller's bearer
identity; it neither creates an administrator identity nor grants permissions.
Its GET settings and POST chat endpoints are `/api/ai-assistant` and
`/api/ai-assistant/chat`. Chat streams `AiAssistantEvent` as SSE and uses
`AiAssistantRequest` with an alternating user/assistant message history ending in
a user message. Page context and historical source references remain untrusted.
Use the public shared UI integration instead of interpreting source references as
arbitrary links or rendering provider output as HTML.

`AiAssistant` also configures shared input/context/output budgets, maximum tool
calls, concurrency, rate and timeout. `InitialOutputTokens` is a per-round starting
budget bounded by `MaxOutputTokens`, not a total billing budget for an entire
conversation. `AiAssistantHttpOptions` supplies report page size and optional
localhost transport settings. Development certificate trust requires Development,
a canonical localhost endpoint and the exact existing Kestrel certificate; do
not disable TLS verification for production. Disabling the feature leaves no
Assistant endpoints and does not resolve provider credentials.

### Independent Assistant acceptance

`AssistantHttpTests` runs the actual API, Keycloak, PostgreSQL, MCP loopback,
Assistant runner and all four published provider adapters. Only vendor responses
are controlled: public named HTTP clients provide SSE/NDJSON fixtures, and Bedrock
uses an anonymous test runtime supplying native Converse stream events. No live
model service, personal AWS credential chain or paid provider request is involved.

The tests verify a real authorized catalog read, explicit sources, unchanged data
and audit, provider token/context budgets, public settings without credentials,
and generic failure responses without provider diagnostics. A reader cannot see
or invoke the equipment tool until granted view permission through the public
security API; anonymous and inactive accounts remain blocked. Oversized or invalid
requests do not reach the provider. Concurrent work is bounded, and both a timeout
and client disconnect cancel the pending provider transport. Configuration tests
verify invalid selected options and cancellation on every native adapter.

These are deterministic integration checks, not live vendor compatibility probes,
model-answer quality evaluations or proof that prompt injection is impossible.
The independent real-agent development evaluations have their own evidence.

Verify opt-out, absent dependency, invalid settings, anonymous/unauthorized access,
disabled capability, malicious content, cancellation and response bounds.
An unsupported business request remains unsupported: do not add platform business
operations, relax permissions or make MCP writable to satisfy an assistant task.

# Persistence, migration packs and performance

Target: NGB 3.4.0. Public contracts:
[Persistence](contracts/NGB.Platform.Persistence.json),
[PostgreSQL](contracts/NGB.Platform.PostgreSql.json) and
[Migrator](contracts/NGB.Platform.Migrator.Core.json).

Keep provider SQL, storage adapters, indexes and migrations in the provider
project. Definitions and Runtime remain independent of PostgreSQL implementation
and HTTP hosting. Use the installed storage interfaces and the scoped
`IUnitOfWork`; it exposes the connection and active transaction explicitly.
Do not open an unrelated transaction inside a document posting strategy.

An `IMigrationPackContributor.GetPacks()` contributes migration packs and their
dependencies. Embed immutable versioned SQL resources, preserve applied checksums
and sequence dependent packs. A new migration must be tested against both empty
storage and a real database containing the supported previous version's state.
Repeating a successful migration must not lose data or reapply business effects.

Treat seed identifiers, role codes and reference data as stable contracts. Seeds
must be idempotent and safe under the documented transaction model. A development
database bootstrap is not evidence of a production upgrade or backup/restore.
Keep deployment migration and rollback decisions separate from CLI file recovery.

Use parameterized SQL and declared table/index shapes. Bound page sizes, batch
writes, row selection, cancellation and reader lifetime. Prefer set-based queries
for lists and reference enrichment; count actual provider calls under realistic
volume. Validate sort stability and cursor/snapshot semantics across pages.

Schema exploration uses the application's approved read-only database tools.
Do not infer permission to alter a live schema from a Kit skill. Run migration and
write tests against isolated resources, never the configured deployment database.

## Migration host and resource identity

The application's Migrator delegates to `PlatformMigratorCli.RunAsync`. Keep
migrations as a separate deployment step and stop the deployment/start sequence
on a nonzero result. The API host does not run migrations automatically.
`--list-modules` and `--dry-run` do not require a connection. Select packs with
`--modules=equipment-inspection`; their dependencies are included and ordered.
`--dry-run --show-scripts` displays the selected resources without connecting.
A normal run requires `--connection` or `NGB_CONNECTION_STRING`. Exit codes are
0 for success, 1 for a migration/plan failure, 2 for missing arguments and 3 for
failure to obtain the schema lock. Explicit skip-lock mode can return success
without applying migrations; it is not evidence that the requested schema exists.

Embedded migration resource names must start with the assembly's name, followed
by `.db.migrations.V` or `.db.migrations.R`. For custom namespaces, set the resource
LogicalName explicitly to `$(AssemblyName).db.migrations.%(Filename)%(Extension)`.
The physical SQL filename and contents remain immutable after application.
`SchemaMigrator` maintains separate histories per pack and runs dependencies
under a schema lock. Its optional repair delegates are a separate mechanism;
do not use them to silently rewrite applied migration history.

The example's `MigrationFixtures/Baseline` freezes four prior application
migrations from an identified package. Its manifest records each SQL hash. The
resource-only fixture projects declare no contributors, so the normal Migrator
does not discover them. Tests select them explicitly through `MigrationPack`.
The matching `IntegrationTests/MigrationBaseline.cs` freezes the definitions and
storage registrations used to seed that schema. It deliberately does not call the
current application's Runtime or Persistence registration methods. Keep this
historical fixture unchanged when adding current fields or contributors.
The baseline is an earlier application schema on SDK 3.4.0; SDK-version upgrade
certification is a separate check. The deliberate ChecksumDrift fixture belongs
only in negative migration acceptance.

If a new field changes the current reader/writer contract, seed the old schema
with the frozen metadata and payload. Then start the current application, verify
every existing value and audit event, and assert the new field's migration value
separately. For other fixtures, keep a base metadata contributor before contributors
that extend its types; replacing a DI registration must retain that ordering.
A fixture that fails while composing definitions has not exercised the migration itself.

## PostgreSQL host composition

Reference `NGB.Platform.PostgreSql` from the provider or host project and register
`services.AddNgbPostgres(connectionString)`. Use
`services.AddPostgres(options => { ... })` when configuring `PostgresOptions`.
Obtain the connection string from server configuration; do not place it in Kit
instructions. A blank string passed to `AddNgbPostgres`, or a null configuration
delegate passed to `AddPostgres`, fails immediately. Options registration also
validates a nonblank connection and `OperationalRegisterPublicationTimeoutSeconds`
in the inclusive range 1–4,294,967 at host startup. This is configuration validation,
not a connectivity check. Command timeout defaults to 30 seconds, advisory-lock
wait to 120 seconds, publication timeout to 5 seconds and detailed errors to false.

Provider registration supplies the scoped `IUnitOfWork`; repeated resolution in
one scope returns the same connection/transaction owner, while another scope has
a different connection. Registration, scope creation and host startup alone do
not open a connection or provision/migrate a database. Execute supported operations
inside their documented transaction boundary. Commit without an active transaction
is an invariant failure. A `TimeProvider` registered before the provider is retained.

The provider registers its standard repositories, readers, writers, schema services,
report execution pipeline and metadata/relation caches. Their concrete public
classes are implementations, not additional business extension bases. Consume
persistence abstractions in provider code and authorized application services at
interactive boundaries. For custom storage use the public type-storage contracts;
for custom report datasets contribute `IPostgresReportDatasetSource`. Copying
platform SQL, replacing authorization with a repository call or mutating provider
caches is not part of those extension workflows.

`PostgresCompositionTests` verifies options, application-clock preservation and
scoped connection ownership using a deliberately unreachable test connection.
It performs no database I/O. Migration and real transactional behavior have their
own independent acceptance cases.

## Typed schema validation and posted-document guards

Application migrations run after the platform pack, so the platform's initial
guard installation cannot see tables created later by the application. After
creating typed `doc_*` head/part tables with `document_id`, call the existing
`ngb_install_typed_document_immutability_guards()` function in a new application
migration. Repeat that installation in a later migration when adding another
typed table. Keep prior applied SQL and checksums unchanged.

The installed `trg_posted_immutable` guard rejects typed INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE while
the registry document is Posted (SQLSTATE 55000). It supplements public lifecycle
and authorization checks; do not use trusted storage as a user-facing bypass.
The independent negative test deliberately invokes `IDocumentTypeStorage` inside
an isolated transaction and confirms that rejection preserves payload, child rows
and audit. Normal public Unpost and subsequent Draft editing still succeed.

Use the exact provider type contract when writing physical migrations. For
3.4.0, `ColumnType.String` maps to `text`; the schema validator does not accept
`character varying` as its alias. Retain `MaxLength` in metadata and use an explicit
`CHECK (char_length(column) <= limit)` when the database must enforce that limit.
The example's additive migration converts existing text values without truncation
and retains their length bounds. Hybrid part tables must also have a direct
`document_id -> documents(id)` foreign key. A cascading foreign key to their typed
head can remain alongside it to own Draft cleanup.

Run `platform.schema.validate` through trusted maintenance composition after
migration and Setup, before lifecycle or report tests. It checks more than
successful application startup: guards, physical types and metadata relationships
must agree. The example retains its
frozen earlier migration fixture and verifies upgrade, repeat execution and
preserved records/audit with these additional migrations.

A test host can resolve `ICatalogSchemaValidationService` and
`IDocumentSchemaValidationService` in an application DI scope and call
`ValidateAllAsync()` on each immediately after migration and Setup. This verifies
the typed application schema before HTTP tests; it does not replace the maintenance
job's additional core-schema checks. The independent agent acceptance host does
this even when generated tests omit schema validation.


## Trusted persistence data shapes

Provider ports exchange storage data after the application service has selected
and authorized the operation. A page record, display label or filter object does
not carry a current-user permission check.

`CatalogHeadDescriptor` and `DocumentHeadDescriptor` describe registered physical
tables and columns. Construct them from trusted Definitions metadata, validate
query filter keys and keep identifiers out of user-controlled input. Catalog
filters use equality against the column's text representation. Document filters
carry their value type; `DocumentPeriodFilter` uses inclusive date boundaries.
`SoftDeleteFilterMode` selects all, active or marked records without granting
permission to change deletion marks.

The `*HeadQueryPage` shapes carry a total; `*HeadSeekPage` also carries explicit
continuation state and may omit a total. Preserve the query's filter/sort contract
when moving to another page. `CatalogHeadValue`, `CatalogHeadWriteRow` and
`DocumentHeadValue` are typed write inputs consumed inside the service's unit of
work. They are not alternatives to Draft validation or document lifecycle rules.

Administrative chart, identity/role and General Journal Entry page records expose
the projections required by their existing services. Their direct repository
interfaces remain trusted server code. Keep application entry points behind the
corresponding permission-aware service. Batch reference labels and
`DocumentDisplayRef` enrich already-selected records; a display name is not proof
of access to the referenced object.

`DimensionSetWrite` carries append-only canonical dimension-set items in the
posting transaction. Relationship cycle/cardinality check records describe
proposed edges; registered direction/cardinality rules and authorized services
still control whether those edges can be created.

Posting-log `PostingOperation` and begin outcomes differ from document action
execution receipts. Posting diagnostics carry bounded pages, status/age and
descending start-time/document/operation continuation. A stale diagnostic does
not itself authorize replay or repair. Outbox consumer statuses likewise describe
delivery state; they do not promise exactly-once handler effects. Preserve the
existing transactional/idempotent handler and retry contracts.

## Existing provider ports and their owners

The following interfaces are trusted persistence boundaries used by the standard
services. Their presence does not certify an alternative provider, every optional
batch path or a performance claim. Use them only within their owning service's
transaction and validation contract.

| Port family | Owner and required semantics |
| --- | --- |
| Catalog registry, universal writer and type storage | Runtime owns validation, display, deletion marks and audit. `ICatalogTypeStorage` initializes/cleans typed rows inside that transaction; the registry remains separate. |
| Document registry and operation state | The lifecycle coordinator locks common headers, increments versions and preserves immutable history. Technical state cleanup is not a public reset operation. |
| Document numbering | Reserve per type/fiscal year inside the transaction; a rollback must not consume the reserved sequence. |
| Built-in journal storage | The journal service owns approval, Draft editing, reversal and due-date execution. Repository reads do not grant these actions. |
| Dimension sets and display enrichment | Canonical sets are append-only and idempotent; labels enrich authorized selections. A label is not an access check. |
| Operational register metadata and movements | Preserve normalized identity, resource/dimension immutability, register locks, append-only movements and provider-assigned IDs. Unpost appends storno. |
| Operational projections and finalization | Monthly net aggregation differs from cumulative balances. Publish derived rows and Finalized together. A prepared result is single-use and cannot outlive its transaction. |
| Reference-register metadata and records | Preserve append-only versions and tombstones. Independent writes require key serialization and command deduplication in the record transaction. |
| Security repositories | Authorized administration owns role protection, active-account checks, access-version invalidation and provisioning compensation. A direct repository mutation does not perform those service checks. |
| Attachments, notes and audit | Parent-authorized services own access, feature flags and content lifetime; metadata persistence is only one part of that workflow. |

Reference-register historical reads distinguish recorded time from effective time.
Write-time selection deliberately has no historical recorded-time cutoff and
requires a key-locked transaction. Visible-page scans may examine tombstones;
preserve the runtime's last-examined-key continuation instead of treating the last
visible record as the full scan boundary. Recorder tombstones must cover all
effective versions, including future-effective buckets.

`IDocumentOperationStateRepository` and register write-state repositories describe
technical lifecycle coordination. They differ from `IDocumentActionExecutionRepository`
and its stored HTTP action result. `Completed` is not current-user authorization;
the action dispatcher refreshes permissions and checks current source/action and
created-document access before returning a completed result.

`AccountingBalanceProjectionResult` reports total violation counts and a sample
list. The sample length is not the total. Likewise, monthly activity/turnover reads
do not authorize repair, closing or reopening. Those operations retain their
existing service boundaries.

## Transactions, locks and maintenance ports

`UnitOfWorkTransactionExtensions` makes ownership explicit. Owned mode rejects
an already active transaction, then begins, commits or rolls back. External mode
requires an active transaction and leaves completion to its caller. Do not catch
a failed business write and commit its caller-owned transaction as success.

Advisory locks belong inside the transaction. The deterministic helpers normalize
month keys, deduplicate/sort keys, and use the optional batch port or sequential
fallback. Finalization publication has a separate register-then-month lock order
and requires a deadline. A lock is concurrency control, not user authorization.

Schema inspection returns a bulk snapshot; optional snapshot scopes share it
within a bounded validation batch and leave standalone reads fresh. Type mappers
compare logical column types with provider types. Neither inspecting a schema
nor generating an `IDdlObject` authorizes changing a deployed database. Use the
existing migrator/provisioning workflow and keep its credentials out of evidence.

Accounting entry writers, closed-period markers and posting-state repositories
are trusted implementation ports. Derived-row rebuilds and the fiscal-reopen
service's narrow closing-journal deletion have explicit transaction/period
owners; they are not general history-edit operations. Technical Completed state
does not establish current-user access. Clear it only as part of the existing
opposite lifecycle transition.

Register write engines coordinate append-only movement/record history, locks,
deduplication and projection dirtiness. Directly marking a month Finalized does
not rebuild its projections. Use the existing runner. The retained legacy
`IOperationalRegisterMonthFinalizer` is adapted internally; new contributions use
`IOperationalRegisterMonthProjector`. A missing register-specific projector is
valid when a default projector is registered. `BlockedNoProjector` means both
paths are unavailable.

These reviewed provider/service contracts describe existing ownership. They do
not certify a new provider, optional batch throughput or arbitrary production
workloads. Keep the independent example's concrete acceptance scope distinct
from the broader public declaration inventory.

## Provider implementation contracts

Combined page/count and seek readers are optional provider optimizations under
the existing authorized catalog/document services. Universal readers, writers,
relationship repositories and physical-schema health readers do not independently
authorize their input. Register metadata and SQL source records contain trusted
physical names and bindings; they are not safe user-selected SQL definitions.

Runtime write engines dispatch to typed storage inside the owning UnitOfWork.
An `InMemory*TypeStorageResolver` keeps registered handlers in memory, not business
records. Keep lifecycle validation, actor access and transaction ownership in the
application service. Direct storage calls cannot substitute for those checks.

Provider bootstrap can provision a database and run migration/repair modes under
its existing locks. Production application hosts use `None` with a dedicated
migrator. Database creation and repair need an explicit operational workflow and
credentials for that workflow; startup failure alone is not an instruction to
repair. Reuse platform lock services and stable advisory-lock namespaces rather
than inventing keys that may fail to coordinate with other hosts.

`PostgresDocumentFilterSql` binds typed values and quotes configured identifiers.
Its SQL expressions, aliases and parameter names must still come from trusted
provider code. Parameterized values do not make caller-supplied expressions safe.
The example uses `PostgresHeadDocumentTypeStorage` for configured head columns;
that adapter is not a generic implementation of arbitrary document part tables.

# Interrupted tooling transactions

Kit synchronization and application upgrades share one operation lock and a
transaction journal. Before replacing files, the CLI stores their original and
incoming bytes under `.ngb/transactions/<id>/objects/`, checks their SHA-256 hashes,
and writes `.ngb/transaction.json`. Completed receipts stay in that transaction
directory. Keep this private recovery directory until the update has been reviewed.

A handled write failure restores the files already changed. An abrupt process
exit can leave a prepared transaction and an operation lock. Inspect it with:

```sh
node infrastructure/ngb.mjs recover --format json
```

The preview does not modify application files. After reviewing the listed paths,
run `node infrastructure/ngb.mjs recover --apply`. A prepared transaction rolls
back; a transaction whose commit or rollback finished only needs its receipt
archived. Running recovery again is harmless.

Recovery verifies all backup bytes before writing, checks that every current file
still matches either its original or incoming hash, and restores original file
permissions. Subsequent edits, missing/corrupt backups, symlinks and unknown
journal fields stop recovery without overwriting the conflicting work. Preserve
that work separately and compare it with the saved bytes before resolving it.

Automatic lock recovery requires a recorded owner on this machine whose process
has exited. A running or reused process ID, a foreign host or a lock without an
owner requires manual inspection; do not delete a lock while another operation
may still be active. Process-crash recovery does not replace filesystem backups
or promise recovery from storage corruption or power loss.

The journal covers source/package/tooling files only. It never rolls back a
database migration or changes a running deployment. Deployment retains its
separate tested-backup requirement.

# Operational and reference registers

Target: NGB 3.4.0. Inspect the artifact-derived
[OperationalRegisters](contracts/NGB.Platform.OperationalRegisters.json),
[ReferenceRegisters](contracts/NGB.Platform.ReferenceRegisters.json),
[Definitions](contracts/NGB.Platform.Definitions.json) and
[Runtime](contracts/NGB.Platform.Runtime.json) symbol inventories.

The two engines have different semantics. Select the engine from the business
requirement before modeling dimensions and resources. Register definitions and
provider schema through public contracts; keep physical storage in PostgreSQL.
Do not create a substitute generic effects table.

For document-driven Operational Registers, implement
`IDocumentOperationalRegisterPostingHandler.BuildMovementsAsync(DocumentRecord,
IOperationalRegisterMovementsBuilder, CancellationToken)`. The handler's TypeCode
must match its document definition. Supply movements for Post/Repost. The existing
engine handles Unpost with appended storno movements; do not delete old movements.

Unpost appends opposite-sign copies only for unmatched stored movements, retaining
their original occurrence dates, dimensions and resources. Repeated corrections
grow history linearly with the effects written; old redundant history remains
unchanged. Sum resources with the `IsStorno` sign, never infer a current amount
from the physical row count. A date change invalidates affected and tracked later
monthly projections. Read published turnovers/balances after normal finalization,
or use the supported resource-net reader for current transaction-visible nets.

For document-driven Reference Registers, implement
`IDocumentReferenceRegisterPostingHandler.BuildRecordsAsync(DocumentRecord,
ReferenceRegisterWriteOperation, IReferenceRegisterRecordsBuilder,
CancellationToken)`. The operation is significant: Post, Repost and Unpost can
require different records. Reference-register history is append-only; a logical
deletion is represented by the supported tombstone semantics, not physical removal.
`IReferenceRegisterIndependentWriteService` is a separate write path; do not use it
to bypass the document lifecycle or its transaction.
Read [independent writes and temporal semantics](independent-reference-registers.md)
for transaction ownership, command identity, periodic buckets, as-of bounds and
tombstone-aware paging. Its example exercises public services in a trusted fixture;
application HTTP/UI authorization remains a separate responsibility.

In 3.4.0 the standard PostgreSQL provider distinguishes automatic cancellation
from intentional deletion for periodic `SubordinateToRecorder` registers. Its
internal `__is_recorder_cancellation` column is not a resource or a public DTO
member: handlers keep the existing contracts and must not populate this flag.
Readers resolve the latest recorded version per exact effective point before
selecting the active schedule. Moving a replacement to an earlier date must not
let an obsolete cancellation hide it. Explicit deletion still ends the value;
historical recorded-time boundaries and repeated Repost idempotency are preserved.
Post also supersedes points left by an older Unpost. The generic Unpost fallback
pages the full recorder history, including future effective dates. Custom providers
must implement equivalent read/write semantics themselves. Independent and
nonperiodic registers keep their existing contracts. Follow [upgrade rules](upgrades.md#reference-register-migration-in-340)
before running new hosts against an existing database.

For backdated periodic reads, effective time and recorded time are separate.
`SliceLastForEffectiveMomentAsync` can ask for September's value using all
knowledge recorded now; `SliceLastAsync` applies its one timestamp to both
boundaries. Do not interpret records written today as knowledge already available
in September. Supply the recorder ID for subordinate reads; these are not a
global latest-value query across all documents.

Operational register read, projection and finalization contracts and reference
